name: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint
request: Create a small, playable Sky Steps checkpoint parkour game for one player on desktop and touch. Build one coherent short course with three ordered checkpoints, a moving-platform crossing, a clearly marked fall hazard, and a finish. Players must physically traverse it; touching a later checkpoint early must not skip progress. Reaching a checkpoint shows visible activation animation and synchronized confirmation sound. Falling returns the player to the last valid checkpoint without losing progress. Show the current checkpoint and elapsed run time, then a completion result and deliberate replay control. Search Marketplace first for reusable checkpoint, moving-platform and course components, preserving useful existing behavior, visuals, motion and media. Inspect what is included and integrate missing rules rather than replacing working components wholesale. Use Marketplace audio and verify it actually plays. If a suitable component cannot be imported faithfully, record that capability gap. Use compact readable geometry and comfortable jumps; choose reasonable style and layout yourself. No multiplayer, saving, purchases or sprawling map. Success needs native traversal, ordered progression, moving-platform behavior, fall recovery, finish/replay and legible desktop/touch UI. A decorative obstacle scene or a timer alone is insufficient.

spec.title: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint
spec.summary:
A compact solo sky-parkour run contained under the supplied namespace. The course begins on a safe floating spawn island with a bright Start pad, a visible chain of floating steps, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a moving-platform crossing, a high-contrast fall zone below, and a finish arch visible in the distance. In the first minute, the player sees the route and HUD immediately, steps onto Start to begin the timer, learns the comfortable jump spacing, reaches Checkpoint 1, and receives a beacon activation animation plus synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The route then leads through the moving-platform crossing to Checkpoint 2, an ascending final step sequence to Checkpoint 3, and the finish.

Progress is server-authoritative and ordered: only the next checkpoint activates, while touching later checkpoints early has no effect. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint progress or elapsed time. The finish only accepts a player who has activated all three checkpoints. Completion freezes the result time and presents a deliberate Replay button; replay resets the run, progress, timer, character position, checkpoint visuals, and moving-course state where required.

Assumptions chosen from the user's permission to choose reasonable style and layout: the timer starts on physical contact with the Start pad; checkpoint order is Start → 1 → 2 → 3 → Finish; horizontal jumps generally remain around 4–6 studs with broad landing surfaces; the moving platform uses a short, readable route with safe boarding areas; replay is never automatic. The experience has no persistence, purchases, competitive systems, or multiplayer-facing features. Internally, player state is still indexed and cleaned per UserId so respawn and server lifecycle behavior remain safe.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and complete obby/course components must be searched and inspected before implementation decisions. Useful verified geometry, scripts, motion, animation, and media will be retained. Unsupported scripts, missing dependencies, failed audio playback, or behavior that cannot be imported faithfully are explicit capability gaps and do not authorize an unverified procedural substitute.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a clean, optimistic high-altitude aesthetic with compact floating islands and a clearly readable forward route. Main traversable surfaces use pale cloud-white and cool cyan materials; structural undersides use deeper blue-violet tones to give each island a designed silhouette. Checkpoints are tall numbered beacon assemblies with dormant cyan rings and a vivid green-white activated state. The finish is a larger gold-white arch that remains visually distinct from checkpoints.

Compose the course as one shallow rising arc rather than a sprawling straight line. From spawn, the player should see Checkpoint 1 in the near foreground, the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2 at mid-distance, then Checkpoint 3 and the finish as elevated focal points. Keep landing surfaces broad, edge profiles crisp, and decorative elements away from jump paths.

The fall hazard is unmistakable: a broad red-magenta warning volume or plane sits below the course, with luminous warning strips and downward chevrons at exposed transition edges. It must contrast strongly with the cool safe-route palette and remain legible without relying on text alone.

Checkpoint activation should be observable from the player camera: illuminate or recolor the beacon, expand or pulse a ring, and briefly emphasize the checkpoint number. Preserve an imported component's verified animation if it provides equivalent feedback. The confirmation sound begins in the same activation phase as the visible response. Later checkpoints remain visibly dormant until their turn.

The HUD is compact and readable on desktop and touch: a top-center checkpoint label such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3,” a large tabular elapsed time beneath it, and restrained status messaging. On completion, show a centered result card with the final time and a generously sized Replay button suitable for touch. Use strong contrast, safe-area-aware margins, rounded panels, and text sizing that remains readable on narrow phone screens. Do not cover the central jump view during active play.

Players must physically traverse it; touching a later checkpoint early must not skip progress. Reaching a checkpoint shows visible activation animation and synchronized confirmation sound. Falling returns the player to the last valid checkpoint without losing progress. Show the current checkpoint and elapsed run time, then a completion result and deliberate replay control. Search Marketplace first for reusable checkpoint, moving-platform and course components, preserving useful existing behavior, visuals, motion and media. Inspect what is included and integrate missing rules rather than replacing working components wholesale. Use Marketplace audio and verify it actually plays. If a suitable component cannot be imported faithfully, record that capability gap. Use compact readable geometry and comfortable jumps; choose reasonable style and layout yourself. No multiplayer, saving, purchases or sprawling map. Success needs native traversal, ordered progression, moving-platform behavior, fall recovery, finish/replay and legible desktop/touch UI. A decorative obstacle scene or a timer alone is insufficient.

playerExperience.title: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint
playerExperience.summary:
A compact solo sky-parkour run contained under the supplied namespace. The course begins on a safe floating spawn island with a bright Start pad, a visible chain of floating steps, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a moving-platform crossing, a high-contrast fall zone below, and a finish arch visible in the distance. In the first minute, the player sees the route and HUD immediately, steps onto Start to begin the timer, learns the comfortable jump spacing, reaches Checkpoint 1, and receives a beacon activation animation plus synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The route then leads through the moving-platform crossing to Checkpoint 2, an ascending final step sequence to Checkpoint 3, and the finish.

Progress is server-authoritative and ordered: only the next checkpoint activates, while touching later checkpoints early has no effect. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint progress or elapsed time. The finish only accepts a player who has activated all three checkpoints. Completion freezes the result time and presents a deliberate Replay button; replay resets the run, progress, timer, character position, checkpoint visuals, and moving-course state where required.

Assumptions chosen from the user's permission to choose reasonable style and layout: the timer starts on physical contact with the Start pad; checkpoint order is Start → 1 → 2 → 3 → Finish; horizontal jumps generally remain around 4–6 studs with broad landing surfaces; the moving platform uses a short, readable route with safe boarding areas; replay is never automatic. The experience has no persistence, purchases, competitive systems, or multiplayer-facing features. Internally, player state is still indexed and cleaned per UserId so respawn and server lifecycle behavior remain safe.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and complete obby/course components must be searched and inspected before implementation decisions. Useful verified geometry, scripts, motion, animation, and media will be retained. Unsupported scripts, missing dependencies, failed audio playback, or behavior that cannot be imported faithfully are explicit capability gaps and do not authorize an unverified procedural substitute.
playerExperience.visualDirection:
Use a clean, optimistic high-altitude aesthetic with compact floating islands and a clearly readable forward route. Main traversable surfaces use pale cloud-white and cool cyan materials; structural undersides use deeper blue-violet tones to give each island a designed silhouette. Checkpoints are tall numbered beacon assemblies with dormant cyan rings and a vivid green-white activated state. The finish is a larger gold-white arch that remains visually distinct from checkpoints.

Compose the course as one shallow rising arc rather than a sprawling straight line. From spawn, the player should see Checkpoint 1 in the near foreground, the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2 at mid-distance, then Checkpoint 3 and the finish as elevated focal points. Keep landing surfaces broad, edge profiles crisp, and decorative elements away from jump paths.

The fall hazard is unmistakable: a broad red-magenta warning volume or plane sits below the course, with luminous warning strips and downward chevrons at exposed transition edges. It must contrast strongly with the cool safe-route palette and remain legible without relying on text alone.

Checkpoint activation should be observable from the player camera: illuminate or recolor the beacon, expand or pulse a ring, and briefly emphasize the checkpoint number. Preserve an imported component's verified animation if it provides equivalent feedback. The confirmation sound begins in the same activation phase as the visible response. Later checkpoints remain visibly dormant until their turn.

The HUD is compact and readable on desktop and touch: a top-center checkpoint label such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3,” a large tabular elapsed time beneath it, and restrained status messaging. On completion, show a centered result card with the final time and a generously sized Replay button suitable for touch. Use strong contrast, safe-area-aware margins, rounded panels, and text sizing that remains readable on narrow phone screens. Do not cover the central jump view during active play.

playerExperience.assetStrategy:
Begin with complete reusable Model searches for checkpoint systems, moving-platform systems, and compact sky-obstacle courses, because these may include the requested geometry, scripts, motion, activation animation, reset hooks, and sound references. Inspect candidate hierarchies and source code, reject arbitrary HTTP or numeric require dependencies, identify unsupported serialization, and test existing behavior before assigning glue scripts or designing replacements. Preserve useful verified behavior and media rather than rebuilding imported components wholesale.

Audio remains a separate required asset obligation even if a checkpoint component includes it. Prefer captured audio from a retained checkpoint component, then search Marketplace separately if no suitable included cue exists. The chosen sound must retain provenance and pass loading, playback, and listening checks. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed; checkpoint animation should come from an inspectable Model when available. Any necessary authored visual tween or integration may only be decided after inspection establishes that equivalent reusable behavior is absent and the asset pipeline records the sourcing result. Import failures, hidden dependencies, unsupported behavior, or failed audio verification must be reported as capability gaps rather than treated as authorization for a procedural substitute.

--SCRIPTS AND MODELS CREATED BY @EthererElsie (Feel free to credit if this system was helpful :3)
--HERE'S A TUTORIAL ON HOW TO USE THE MOVING PLATFORM SYSTEM AND WHAT EACH VALUE DOES!!!

--Simply there are two parts in the model called Start and Finish, you can move these around as you please, and set the starting positions and ending positions! (P.S, Don't worry about removing the billboardguis or attachments from the parts, they automatically remove themselves once the game starts running, they're simply there to give you a good idea for what it may look like!)
--IF you have a Custom Platform Model you want to use for the platform, simply put it in the PlatformModel folder inside the model, ungroup the your model (if it's grouped), and rename the center part of the model to "Handle" in order for it to work!

--WHAT EACH ATTRIBUTE DOES:
--Now select the MovingPlatform model and open the properties tab and scroll down to the attributes section, the attributes control how the moving platform works!!

--Active - Boolean: The active attribute simply states whether or not the platform is moving or not, if this value is set to true, the platform will move, if it's set to false, it will not move (Setting it to false while the platform is moving will cause it to pause at it's current position unless ResetWhenDeactivated is set to true)
--AlignCFrame - Boolean: This attribute determines if the moving platform's Position and Orientation should align with the Start and End goal CFrames/Orientations
--Delay - Number: Whenever the platform reaches it's certain end and start goals, this value will control how long the platform stops once it reaches it's goal before it continues to move again.
--Direction - String: The Tween Direction of the Platform (Must be set to 'In', 'Out', or 'InOut' or else it won't work) For more info on Tween Directions, visit here: https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/enums/EasingDirection
--GoalReached - Boolean: A value that simply tells you if the platform has hit the end goal, if the Platform is looped, it will swap between these values as it moves back and fourth between the start and end position, if this value is set to true before starting the game, the platform will automatically start at the ending position instead of the starting position
--Length - Number: Simply the amount of time in seconds it takes for the platform to reach it's goal
--MovementType - String: This value makes up how the platform should move, if this value is set to 'Loop' it will always move back and fourth between the start and end position, if it's set to 'LoopOnce' then the platform will move back and fourth between the start and the end position once then it will stop, or if it's set to 'Once' then the platform will move to the end position or start position then completely stop until it is set to active again.
--ResetWhenDeactivated - Boolean: This value determines whether or not the platform will pause at it's current position when it's deactivated or if it resets back to it's starting position when deactivated
--Stick - Boolean: This value simply determines whether or not a player can stick to the platform
--Style - String: The Tween Style of the Platform (Must be set to 'Linear', 'Sine', 'Back', 'Quad', 'Quart', 'Quint', 'Bounce', 'Elastic', 'Exponential', 'Circular', or 'Cubic' or else it won't work) For more info on Tween Styles, visit here: https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/enums/EasingStyle


--AND THAT'S IT!! Hopefully this helps people out!!

local ts = game:GetService("TweenService")
local physics = game:GetService("PhysicsService")
local info = TweenInfo.new
local insert = table.insert

physics:RegisterCollisionGroup("MovingPlatforms")

function getEnum(name, enum)
	for _, v in enum:GetEnumItems() do
		if v.Name == name then
			return v
		end
	end
end

function weldModel(model : Model, canStick : boolean)
	local handle = model:WaitForChild("Handle")
	handle.Anchored = true
	
	for _, v in model:GetDescendants() do
		if v:IsA("BasePart") then
			v.CanCollide = true
			v.CanTouch = true
			v.CollisionGroup = "MovingPlatforms"
			if canStick then
				v:AddTag("___Stick")
			end
			if v ~= handle then
				local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint", v)
				weld.Part0 = v
				weld.Part1 = handle
				weld.Enabled = true
				v.Anchored = false
			end
		end
	end
	
	return handle
end

function checkCFrame(align : boolean, frame : CFrame)
	if align then
		return frame
	else
		return CFrame.new(frame.Position)
	end
end

function setup(platformFolder : Model)
	local platform = platformFolder:WaitForChild("PlatformModel")
	local start, finish = platformFolder:WaitForChild("Start"), platformFolder:WaitForChild("Finish")
	
	local atts = platformFolder:GetAttributes()
	
	local handle = weldModel(platform, atts["Stick"])
	
	local functionsList = {}
	
	insert(functionsList, platformFolder.AttributeChanged:Connect(function()
		atts = platformFolder:GetAttributes()
	end))
	
	if atts["GoalReached"] then
		handle.CFrame = checkCFrame(atts["AlignCFrame"], finish.CFrame)
	else
		handle.CFrame = checkCFrame(atts["AlignCFrame"], start.CFrame)
	end
	
	local goals = {
		goalEnd = {},
		goalStart = {},
		goalReset = {}
	}
	
	goals.goalStart.CFrame = checkCFrame(atts["AlignCFrame"], start.CFrame)
	goals.goalEnd.CFrame = checkCFrame(atts["AlignCFrame"], finish.CFrame)
	goals.goalReset.CFrame = checkCFrame(atts["AlignCFrame"], handle.CFrame)
	
	local tweenFo = info(atts["Length"], getEnum(atts["Style"], Enum.EasingStyle), getEnum(atts["Direction"], Enum.EasingDirection), 0, false, atts["Delay"])
	
	local tweenEnd, tweenStart = ts:Create(handle, tweenFo, goals.goalEnd), ts:Create(handle, tweenFo, goals.goalStart)
	local tweenReset = ts:Create(handle, info(.25), goals.goalReset)
	
	local resetValue = atts["GoalReached"]
	local reset = false
	local looped = true
	
	local debounce = false
	
	local playingStart, playingFinish = false, false
	
	insert(functionsList, platformFolder:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Active"):Connect(function()
		if platformFolder:GetAttribute("Active") then
			if atts["GoalReached"] then
				tweenStart:Play()
			else
				tweenEnd:Play()
			end
			reset = false
		else
			if atts["ResetWhenDeactivated"] then
				reset = true
				looped = true
				tweenReset:Play()
				platformFolder:SetAttribute("GoalReached", resetValue)
			else
				if atts["GoalReached"] then
					tweenStart:Pause()
				else
					tweenEnd:Pause()
				end
			end
		end
	end))
	
	insert(functionsList, tweenStart:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PlaybackState"):Connect(function()
		if tweenStart.PlaybackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Playing and not playingStart then
			playingStart = true
			tweenStart.Completed:Wait()
			if not reset then
				if atts["MovementType"] == "Loop" then
					looped = not looped
					tweenEnd:Play()
				elseif atts["MovementType"] == "LoopOnce" then
					looped = not looped
					if not looped then
						tweenEnd:Play()
					else
						platformFolder:SetAttribute("Active", false)
					end
				elseif atts["MovementType"] == "Once" then
					platform:SetAttribute("Active", false)
				end

				platformFolder:SetAttribute("GoalReached", false)
			end
			playingStart = false
		end
	end))
	
	insert(functionsList, tweenEnd:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PlaybackState"):Connect(function()
		if tweenEnd.PlaybackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Playing and not playingFinish then
			playingFinish = true
			tweenEnd.Completed:Wait()
			if not reset then
				if atts["MovementType"] == "Loop" then
					looped = not looped
					tweenStart:Play()
				elseif atts["MovementType"] == "LoopOnce" then
					looped = not looped
					if not looped then
						tweenStart:Play()
					else
						platformFolder:SetAttribute("Active", false)
					end
				elseif atts["MovementType"] == "Once" then
					platform:SetAttribute("Active", false)
				end

				platformFolder:SetAttribute("GoalReached", true)
			end
			playingFinish = false
		end
	end))
	
	if atts["Active"] then
		if atts["GoalReached"] then
			tweenStart:Play()
		else
			tweenEnd:Play()
		end
	end
	
	start:Destroy()
	finish:Destroy()
	
	insert(functionsList, platformFolder.Destroying:Connect(function()
		for _, func in pairs(functionsList) do
			func:Disconnect()
		end
		tweenStart:Destroy()
		tweenEnd:Destroy()
	end))
end

function check(v)
	if v:IsA("Model") then
		if v:HasTag("MovingPlatform") then
			setup(v)
		end
	end
end

workspace.DescendantAdded:Connect(check)

for _, v in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	check(v)
end

local Char = script.Parent
local Hum = Char:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

local RunS = game:GetService("RunService")

local Params = RaycastParams.new()
Params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {Char}
Params.CollisionGroup = "MovingPlatforms"
Params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude

local runFun, diedFun, LastPlatform, LastPlatformCF, Delta, Platform, ray, Raycast, Hit, currentState

local RootAttach = Char:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart")

local find = table.find

local StateList = {
	"Jumping",
	"FallingDown",
	"Freefall",
	"Landed",
	"Physics"
}

runFun = RunS.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
	if Char and Hum then
		currentState = Hum:GetState()
		if Hum.RootPart and currentState then
			if find(StateList, currentState.Name) then
				return
			end
			
			ray = Vector3.new(0,(-Char:GetExtentsSize().Y/2)-.1,0)

			Raycast = workspace:Raycast(RootAttach.CFrame.Position,ray, Params)
			Hit = nil
			
			if Raycast then
				Hit = Raycast.Instance
			end
			
			if Hit then
				if Hit:HasTag("___Stick") then

					Platform = Hit
					
					if LastPlatformCF ~= nil and LastPlatform == Platform then
						Delta = Platform.CFrame * LastPlatformCF:inverse()
						Delta -= Vector3.new(0, Delta.Position.Y, 0)
						RootAttach.CFrame = Delta*RootAttach.CFrame
					end
					
					LastPlatform = Platform
					LastPlatformCF = Platform.CFrame
					
					return
				end
			end
			
			LastPlatformCF = nil
			LastPlatform = nil
		end
	end
end)

diedFun = Hum.Died:Connect(function()
	runFun:Disconnect()
	diedFun:Disconnect()
	script:Destroy()
end)

		return CFrame.new(cf.Position)
	end
end

local function setup(platformModel: Model)
	if platformModel:GetAttribute("_SetupDone") then return end
	platformModel:SetAttribute("_SetupDone", true)

	local platformFolder = platformModel:WaitForChild("PlatformModel", 5)
	local startPart = platformModel:WaitForChild("Start", 5)
	local finishPart = platformModel:WaitForChild("Finish", 5)

	if not platformFolder or not startPart or not finishPart then
		return
	end

	local function getAttr(key, default)
		local val = platformModel:GetAttribute(key)
		if val == nil then return default end
		return val
	end

	local canStick = getAttr("Stick", true)
	local handle = weldPlatformModel(platformFolder, canStick)
	if not handle then return end

	local alignCFrame = getAttr("AlignCFrame", true)
	local length = getAttr("Length", 4)
	local delayTime = getAttr("Delay", 0.8)
	local styleName = getAttr("Style", "Sine")
	local directionName = getAttr("Direction", "InOut")
	local movementType = getAttr("MovementType", "Loop")

	local startCF = startPart.CFrame
	local finishCF = finishPart.CFrame

	if getAttr("GoalReached", false) then
		handle.CFrame = checkCFrame(alignCFrame, finishCF)
	else
		handle.CFrame = checkCFrame(alignCFrame, startCF)
	end

	local easingStyle = getEasingEnum(styleName, Enum.EasingStyle, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine)
	local easingDirection = getEasingEnum(directionName, Enum.EasingDirection, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut)
	local tweenInfo = TweenInfo.new(length, easingStyle, easingDirection, 0, false, delayTime)

	local tweenEnd = TweenService:Create(handle, tweenInfo, { CFrame = checkCFrame(alignCFrame, finishCF) })
	local tweenStart = TweenService:Create(handle, tweenInfo, { CFrame = checkCFrame(alignCFrame, startCF) })

	local connections = {}
	local isLooping = (movementType == "Loop")

	local function playNext(toFinish)
		if not platformModel.Parent then return end
		if toFinish then
			tweenEnd:Play()
		else
			tweenStart:Play()
		end
	end

	table.insert(connections, tweenEnd.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
		if playbackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and isLooping then
			platformModel:SetAttribute("GoalReached", true)
			playNext(false)
		end
	end))

	table.insert(connections, tweenStart.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
		if playbackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and isLooping then
			platformModel:SetAttribute("GoalReached", false)
			playNext(true)
		end
	end))

	if startPart:IsA("BasePart") then
		startPart.Transparency = 1
		startPart.CanCollide = false
		startPart.CanTouch = false
	end
	if finishPart:IsA("BasePart") then
		finishPart.Transparency = 1
		finishPart.CanCollide = false
		finishPart.CanTouch = false
	end

	if getAttr("Active", true) ~= false then
		playNext(true)
	end

	table.insert(connections, platformModel.Destroying:Connect(function()
		for _, conn in ipairs(connections) do
			conn:Disconnect()
		end
		tweenEnd:Cancel()
		tweenStart:Cancel()
		tweenEnd:Destroy()
		tweenStart:Destroy()
	end))
end

local function onDescendantAdded(desc: Instance)
	if desc:IsA("Model") and (desc.Name == "MovingPlatform" or desc:HasTag("MovingPlatform")) then
		task.defer(setup, desc)
	end
end

workspace.DescendantAdded:Connect(onDescendantAdded)
for _, desc in ipairs(workspace:GetDescendants()) do
	onDescendantAdded(desc)
end

local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local rootPart = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local raycastParams = RaycastParams.new()
raycastParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { character }
raycastParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
pcall(function()
	raycastParams.CollisionGroup = "MovingPlatforms"
end)

local ignoreStates = {
	[Enum.HumanoidStateType.Jumping] = true,
	[Enum.HumanoidStateType.FallingDown] = true,
	[Enum.HumanoidStateType.Freefall] = true,
	[Enum.HumanoidStateType.Physics] = true,
	[Enum.HumanoidStateType.Dead] = true,
}

local lastPlatform: BasePart? = nil
local lastPlatformCF: CFrame? = nil

local heartbeatConn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
	if not character or not humanoid or humanoid.Health <= 0 then return end
	local currentState = humanoid:GetState()
	if ignoreStates[currentState] then
		lastPlatform = nil
		lastPlatformCF = nil
		return
	end

	local rayOrigin = rootPart.Position
	local rayDirection = Vector3.new(0, -3.8, 0)
	local rayResult = workspace:Raycast(rayOrigin, rayDirection, raycastParams)

	if rayResult and rayResult.Instance and rayResult.Instance:HasTag("___Stick") then
		local hitPart = rayResult.Instance
		if lastPlatform == hitPart and lastPlatformCF then
			local delta = hitPart.CFrame * lastPlatformCF:Inverse()
			local deltaPos = delta.Position
			local deltaRot = delta - deltaPos
			rootPart.CFrame = CFrame.new(deltaPos.X, 0, deltaPos.Z) * deltaRot * rootPart.CFrame
		end
		lastPlatform = hitPart
		lastPlatformCF = hitPart.CFrame
	else
		lastPlatform = nil
		lastPlatformCF = nil
	end
end)

humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
	heartbeatConn:Disconnect()
	script:Destroy()
end)
